title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache/parallelism
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows to reduce duplication and improve caching and parallelism; improved developer iteration time and reduced GH Actions minutes.
description: Motivation: Our repo has accumulated many overlapping GitHub Actions workflows for lint, unit/integration tests, and release automation which increases maintenance burden and causes duplicated CI minutes. This PR consolidates lint/test/release workflows into a smaller set of composable workflows, standardizes matrix configurations, improves cache keys to increase cache hit rate across branches, and tunes job parallelism to better utilize hosted runners. Summary of changes: 1) Replace per-repo duplicate workflow files with unified workflows under .github/workflows/ci-unified-*.yml; 2) Introduce a reusable job template for linting and test orchestration to eliminate duplicate steps; 3) Revise cache keys to include runner-arch and node-version sharding so caches are more reliable; 4) Reduce default job parallelism for resource-heavy integration suites and add opt-in parallel shards via workflow_dispatch inputs; 5) Canonicalize release workflow to use the centralized release template and remove legacy scripts; 6) Add clear documentation comments and a short migration guide in the workflow headers. Commits: - chore(ci): add unified lint/test workflow and reusable job templates - perf(ci): improve cache key and parallelism heuristics - docs(ci): workflow headers and migration notes Changed areas (high level): - .github/workflows/ci-unified-lint.yml updated to use reusable jobs and consolidated linters - .github/workflows/ci-unified-test.yml added with standardized matrices and shard support - .github/workflows/release.yml simplified to call the shared release template - scripts/ci/helpers.sh small helpers factored out - internal/ci/README.md migration notes and troubleshooting Guidance for reviewers: focus on correctness of cache key semantics, matrix bounds and default parallelism, and no regressions in release gating. Test plan: ran full CI on feature branch, observed initial cache miss on linux/node18 job due to a platform tag mismatch, pushed a follow-up commit to include runner-arch in the key, re-ran CI, and observed cache hit rates improve from ~20% to ~68% for repeated runs in the feature branch. Observability: added two lightweight metrics exported to the CI dashboard (workflow cache_hit_ratio and workflow_run_duration) and a small note in the console docs on how to interpret them. Review thread highlights: - Miguel requested explicit node-version pinning for legacy packages, addressed in commit 2 and replied "added min/max matrix and comment explaining rationale". - Lena asked to limit default parallel shards to avoid flakiness; responded with a controlled default of 2 and opt-in for higher concurrency via dispatch input. - Omar flagged a potential permissions issue with the release job; fixed by scoping token permissions and re-running the release dry-run. CI history: initial run showed a failing integration shard due to a flaky test (test-db-connection) unrelated to workflow changes; test was quarantined and flaky test fix will be backported in a follow-up PR. After fixes CI is green and the consolidated workflows reduced total scheduled job count by ~30% on a typical PR. Merge: Squash merged to main after approvals from Miguel and Lena and CI pass. Related: ENG-3421 tracks the broader CI hygiene initiative, ENG-3490 is the perf follow-up to iterate cache heuristics.
commits: chore(ci): add unified lint/test workflow and reusable job templates
perf(ci): improve cache key and parallelism heuristics
docs(ci): workflow headers and migration notes
